source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

TASK: Write an ORIGINAL short prose passage in English, set in the target scenario below. It must be

specified below while inventing entirely new words and moving the content into the target

Reproduce, period by period, the CLAUSE-NESTING SCHEMA below --- an indented tree in which each line is a clause (main / relative / adverbial / complement / coordinate) and indentation marks subordination (a clause indented under another is embedded in it). The WORD ORDER and the words themselves are entirely yours; only the clause-embedding tree is fixed.

TARGET SCENARIO --- render the content here (in your own words):
  - a supermarket checkout line at a busy hour
  - the conveyor belt, the barcode scanner, the bagging area, the card reader
  - the cashier and a shopper; a cart, a divider bar, a receipt
  - another shopper crowding from behind; a small friction over space in the queue
  - the register of retail routine: beeps, the total announced, loyalty-card prompts

REQUIREMENTS --- both hold together:
1. CLAUSE NESTING PRESERVED --- the same clause-embedding tree per period (which clause embeds in which, to the same depth), in any word order and words you choose.
2. COHERENT --- one continuous, fully sensible passage in the target scenario; new lexicon,
   no trace of any source content.

Write modern, natural English. Produce the 10 periods in order as continuous prose --- no
numbering, no headings. Output ONLY the passage: no preamble, no self-audit.

gens.text: The line snakes long, carts loaded heavy. To scan each item quickly, the cashier works to beat the rush, her hands a blur. Beep. A divider slides, marking boundaries. Behind, a shopper edges closer, space tight and tempers thin. Bags wait, ready to fill. Overhead, the card reader blinks, awaiting the final swipe. The total chimes, a number called out loud. Loyalty cards flash, discounts promised. In the chaos, a receipt prints, proof of purchase. Transactions complete, the cycle repeats.

The line snakes through the store, carts brimming.  
Shoppers load items, waiting to pay, as the conveyor belt slides forward.  
Beeps punctuate the air.  
The cashier scans each item, her hands moving swiftly.  
Behind her, the bagging area fills quickly, bags piling high.  
A customer taps the card reader, eyes on the screen.  
Another shopper shifts, impatient, in the line behind.  
The register chimes, announcing the total.  
The cashier asks for a loyalty card, her voice steady.  
A receipt prints, the paper curling slightly.

The line snakes forward, carts piled high with evening buys. The scanner whirs to life, awaiting items to glide across its beam, while the cashier greets the shopper with a practiced smile. The conveyor belt hums, a steady stream of goods passing through. A woman, her cart overflowing, eyes the space warily. She inches closer, the divider bar clinking softly against the belt. The beeps of the scanner punctuate the air, each product registered with a chime. The total mounts, displayed prominently on the screen. The cashier prompts for a loyalty card, the machine ready to read. The next shopper, impatient, leans in, causing a slight tension in the queue. The receipt prints, a final confirmation of the day’s purchases.
